newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude under pressure from unsold barrels.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude under pressure from unsold barrels.

text.p: Wet Brent markets were quiet in early trade on Wednesday with premiums still under pressure from an overhang of prompt June barrels, traders said.
Markets showed little reaction to last night's American Petroleum Institute inventory data which brokers said were mostly neutral.
Inter-month spreads on the cash market were steady to a shade weaker, July/August losing a cent to trade at -32 cents.

Short-term swaps were slightly weaker. Bids for contract for differences for June 11-13 against August Brent slipped five cents to -$1.00, while June 16-20 was steady against August at -80/-74 cents, brokers said.

Although outright values were showing some recovery from year-lows hit late on Tuesday the weight of unsold cargoes and a tight transatlantic arbitrage were keeping things bleak for North Sea sellers.
"There are still lots of June grades, including Brent, not yet committed with no end-users buying and refiners already committed," said one trader. "Most probably premiums will drop again."
Mild relief might come in the form of buying for storage to take advantage of the steep price contango but some traders questioned how much tankage was available.
In late trades on Monday a 24-26 June loading Oseberg was heard done at dated Brent -10 cents, 5 cents weaker than earlier that day. Two late June loading Ekofisk cargoes were traded at dated even.
